newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market lifeless amid peso jitters.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market lifeless amid peso jitters.

text.p: The secondary market in Treasury bills saw little trading amid the volatility in the currency market, dealers said.
"The government securities market is dead as expected," a trader said.
"You don't know when the 32 percent overnight rate of the Central Bank will last. The carrying cost is too high," he added.
Last week, the Central Bank raised its overnight rate to a two-and-a-half year high of 32 percent to stave off speculation against the peso.

The peso continued to be volatile after the Central Bank said it would loosen its hold on the currency to seek its own level. The peso succumbed to overwhelming pressure last week from speculators who believed it was overvalued like the Thai baht.
Traders said they expected an increase of at least 150 basis points in the auction later. At the same time, tenders may also be rejected by the auction committee, they said.
The average interbank call loan rate rose to 32.375 percent from 32.15625 percent as banks covered weekend positions.
The rate had soared to a high of 38 percent even though lenders outnumbered borrowers 39 to 20.
Traders said small banks were constrained to borrow at such rate because of the Central Bank's high rates.
Turnover swelled to 31.35 billion pesos from 9.55 billion pesos.
